pr.body:
A source can become sensitive while a dream candidate is being published. The final database write correctly rejects the stale source, but the dream cycle still counted a promotion, and public graph and raw recall could return the staged memory. This change reports the failed publication accurately and keeps the candidate hidden until publication completes.

The cycle now counts applied publications. Failed attempts carry the returned denial reason and no promoted ID in both the candidate receipt and audit event. Dry runs retain their recommendation while reporting zero applied promotions and recording a review event.

Both final recall gates use the protected validation association to require a promoted capture with a matching entity pointer. Reserving a critic binding alone is insufficient. Pending capture access remains available to the publisher and administrative readers, so normal finalization continues to work. The change requires no schema migration.

## 🧪 Validation

The concurrent source-policy regression fails before the fix and passes afterward against isolated SurrealDB 3.2.3. Independent native controls cover public graph get/list and raw recall during pending publication, denied publication, successful completion, and replay. Additional tests reject missing or mismatched publication pointers.

Independent review passed with 3 native visibility controls, 17 native publication tests, 12 graph-read batching tests, 8 receipt tests, and core/API lint and type checking. Root repeated the 3 independent controls and quality checks. The earlier reflection verification passed all 43 cases across five suites. Integration review passed after rebasing onto the merged packet pipeline; root repeated the 4 native visibility/packet controls and quality gates on the final head.

A broader local core run passed 4,574 tests but was not green: eight tests encountered the harness DNS guard, and one concurrent-read fixture still represented a pending capture as published. The fixture is corrected; its full 12-test module passes. All applicable [hosted CI checks](https://github.com/hyperb1iss/sibyl/actions/runs/34807987124) passed on the integrated head, including the full core and API suites. The [local-embedding runtime smoke](https://github.com/hyperb1iss/sibyl/actions/runs/34807987008) passed as well.

local_readiness.conclusion: The observed blocking boundary is OrbStack host-to-guest forwarding and guest service availability. The API process remains responsive, but its database endpoint and the Docker API do not return responses.
confirmed: Local API is running commit 1ffeeda1790ad45812b225f5d2aad686f2fe3e2e. Reloader parent PID 58477 and worker PID 58597 own port 3334 from the local apps/api checkout.
Paired probes: API liveness returned HTTP 200 in 9 ms; API readiness and direct SurrealDB health each accepted TCP in less than 1 ms and returned no response bytes before 5 s.
OrbStack Helper PID 2302 owns both IPv4 and IPv6 port 8000 listeners. Its observed FD inventory included 1,304 CLOSED port 8000 connections, 1,504 total FDs and 155 threads.
The Docker orbstack context is selected. Docker ps failed to return within 6 s; orbctl status answered Running, which does not establish guest or database health.
Current OrbStack vmgr logs repeatedly report host-tcp forward dial failures to guest endpoint 0.250.250.2:44465 with context deadline exceeded.
API native samples show the event loop sleeping in uvloop/kevent, with no sampled SurrealKV execution or CPU-bound database work. The helper sample is mostly unsymbolized waits.
limits: The guest Docker API is unavailable, so no database process stack, query latency, lock ownership or container inventory could be inspected.
The FD accumulation is an observation, not proof that an FD limit or leak caused the outage. No internal OrbStack lock or guest kernel failure has been identified.

The readiness endpoint connects a dedicated auth client before checking coordination. The direct database failure explains why readiness can stall, but no suspended Python coroutine stack was collected.

PR #590 changes schema setup and embedding repair; it changes none of the inspected readiness/auth connection/log route owners. No evidence shows that updating the checkout repairs this transport failure.
local_readiness.next_boundary: Root should evaluate recovery of the shared OrbStack guest/service path separately, preserving other workloads. Direct database health and API readiness must pass before considering any separately authorized pending-write replay.
